text:
# Getting started with Nimbus

Nimbus is a team task and time-tracking app. To get started, sign up at app.nimbus.example with a work email, verify the email, then create your first workspace. A workspace holds your projects, tasks, and team members. After creating a workspace you are the workspace Owner. Invite teammates from Settings > Members. New workspaces start on the free Starter plan, which supports up to 3 members and 2 active projects. You can create your first project from the Projects tab by clicking New Project.

# Creating an account

Create an account at app.nimbus.example by clicking Sign Up. You can sign up with an email and password, or with Google or Microsoft single sign-on. Email signups must verify their address within 24 hours or the signup link expires. If the verification email does not arrive, check spam and confirm the address is correct, then use Resend verification on the login screen. One email can belong to multiple workspaces.

# Resetting your password

To reset your password, go to the login screen and click Forgot password. Enter your account email and we send a reset link that is valid for 60 minutes. Open the link and choose a new password of at least 10 characters with one number. If the link expired, request a new one. Accounts created with Google or Microsoft SSO do not have a Nimbus password; sign in through that provider instead. Reset links can only be used once.

# Fixing login problems

If you cannot log in, first confirm you are using the correct email. Common causes are a caps-lock password, a browser autofilling an old password, or an account that uses SSO. After five failed attempts the account is locked for 15 minutes as a security measure. If you see 'account not found', you may be trying to log into the wrong region; Nimbus has separate EU and US logins. Clearing cookies for app.nimbus.example fixes most stuck-login problems.

# Plans and pricing

Nimbus has three plans. Starter is free: up to 3 members, 2 active projects, 30-day history. Team is 9 USD per member per month: unlimited projects, unlimited history, integrations, and reports. Business is 18 USD per member per month: everything in Team plus SSO, advanced permissions, and audit logs. Annual billing gives two months free. Prices are per member and are billed for the members active on your workspace during the billing period.

# Upgrading or downgrading your plan

Change your plan from Settings > Billing > Change plan. Upgrades take effect immediately and we charge a prorated amount for the rest of the current billing period. Downgrades take effect at the end of the current period, so you keep paid features until then. Downgrading to Starter is blocked if your workspace exceeds the Starter limits (more than 3 members or more than 2 active projects); remove members or archive projects first.

# Invoices and receipts

Every payment generates an invoice you can download from Settings > Billing > Invoices as a PDF. Invoices list the plan, the number of billed members, the period, and any proration. To add a company name, tax ID, or billing address to future invoices, edit the billing details on the same page before your next charge; invoices already issued cannot be edited. Only workspace Owners and Admins can see billing.

# Refund policy

Nimbus offers a full refund within 14 days of a new paid subscription or an upgrade charge. After 14 days, charges are non-refundable, but you can cancel to stop future charges. Prorated upgrade charges follow the same 14-day window. Refunds return to the original payment method within 5 to 10 business days. To request a refund, contact support with the invoice number from Settings > Billing > Invoices.

# Canceling your subscription

Cancel from Settings > Billing > Cancel subscription. Cancellation stops future charges and moves the workspace to the free Starter plan at the end of the current paid period, so you keep paid features until then. Your data is not deleted when you cancel. If you exceed Starter limits after the period ends, projects beyond the limit become read-only until you upgrade again or archive them. Only the Owner can cancel.

# Payment methods

Nimbus accepts major credit and debit cards and, on annual Business plans, invoice payment by bank transfer. Add or update a card in Settings > Billing > Payment method. If a charge fails, we retry three times over five days and email the Owner and Admins. After the final failed retry the workspace moves to a limited state until a working card is added. We do not store full card numbers; payments are handled by our payment provider.

# Inviting team members

Invite people from Settings > Members > Invite. Enter their email and pick a role. They receive an invite link valid for 7 days. Pending invites count toward your plan's member limit only after they accept. On the free Starter plan you can have up to 3 members total including yourself. To invite in bulk, paste multiple emails separated by commas. You can revoke a pending invite from the same page.

# Roles and permissions

Nimbus has four roles. Owner: full control including billing and deleting the workspace; there is exactly one Owner. Admin: manage members, projects, and settings, but not billing unless granted. Member: create and work on tasks in projects they belong to. Guest: view and comment only, and only in projects they are added to. Advanced per-project permissions are available on the Business plan. Change a person's role from Settings > Members.

# Transferring workspace ownership

The current Owner can transfer ownership from Settings > Members by choosing Make Owner on an Admin. There can only be one Owner, so the previous Owner becomes an Admin. Ownership transfer also moves billing responsibility. The new Owner must already be a member of the workspace. This action cannot be undone by anyone except the new Owner transferring it back.

# Creating and managing projects

Create a project from the Projects tab with New Project. Give it a name, an optional color, and choose which members can access it. Projects hold tasks, sections, and a timeline. On the free Starter plan you can have 2 active projects; archived projects do not count. Archive a project from its settings menu to keep its data without it counting toward limits. Only Owners and Admins can delete a project, which is permanent.

# Archiving vs deleting a project

Archiving hides a project and stops it counting toward plan limits, but keeps all its tasks and time entries; you can restore it anytime from Projects > Archived. Deleting a project permanently removes it and all its tasks and time entries after a 7-day grace period, during which an Admin can restore it from Projects > Recently deleted. After 7 days deletion is final and cannot be reversed.

# Working with tasks

Add a task inside a project with the New Task button or by pressing N. A task has a title, an optional assignee, a due date, a status, and subtasks. Assign a task by typing @ and the person's name. Set a due date from the calendar picker. Drag tasks between sections to change status. Completed tasks stay searchable. You can only assign tasks to members who have access to that project.

# Subtasks and dependencies

Break a task into subtasks from the task detail panel; each subtask can have its own assignee and due date. A parent task shows a progress bar based on completed subtasks. Dependencies (this task is blocked by another) are available on the Team and Business plans. A task marked blocked shows a red indicator and will not send a due-soon reminder until it is unblocked.

# Tracking time

Track time on any task with the built-in timer. Open a task and click Start timer, or press T to start the timer on the selected task. Only one timer runs at a time; starting a new timer stops the previous one. Stop the timer to save a time entry. You can also add time manually with Add time entry by entering a duration and date. Time entries belong to the person who logged them.

# Editing and correcting time entries

Edit a time entry from the task's Time tab: change its duration, date, or note, or delete it. You can edit your own entries anytime. Admins can edit any member's entries. If a timer was left running by mistake, stop it, then edit the entry's duration to the correct value. Deleted time entries cannot be recovered, so edit rather than delete when unsure.

# Timesheets

The Timesheet view shows tracked time per person per day for a project or the whole workspace, available on Team and Business plans. Switch between week and month views. Admins can see everyone's timesheet; members see their own. Approve timesheets, if approvals are enabled in Settings > Time, by clicking Approve on a week. Approved weeks lock their time entries from further edits by members.

# Reports and exporting data

Reports (Team and Business plans) summarize time and task completion by project, person, or date range. Export any report to CSV from the Export button. You can also export a project's full task list to CSV from the project menu. Exports include only data you have permission to see. Large exports are prepared in the background and emailed as a download link that expires after 24 hours.

# Slack integration

Connect Slack from Settings > Integrations > Slack (Team and Business plans). After authorizing, choose which channel receives notifications and which events to post, such as task assigned or task completed. You can also create a task from Slack with the /nimbus command. Disconnecting Slack stops notifications but does not remove any tasks. Each workspace connects to one Slack workspace at a time.

# Google Calendar integration

Sync task due dates to Google Calendar from Settings > Integrations > Google Calendar. Tasks with a due date appear as all-day events on a dedicated Nimbus calendar. The sync is one-way: changes in Nimbus update the calendar, but editing the calendar event does not change the task. Sync runs every 15 minutes. If events look out of date, use Resync now on the integration page.

# Zapier and webhooks

Automate Nimbus with Zapier or raw webhooks (Team and Business plans). Triggers include task created, task completed, and time entry added; actions include create task and add time entry. Generate a webhook signing secret in Settings > Integrations > Webhooks and verify the signature on your endpoint. Webhooks retry failed deliveries for up to 24 hours. Use these to connect Nimbus to tools we do not integrate with directly.

# Getting and using API keys

Create an API key from Settings > Developer > API keys (Team and Business plans). A key inherits your own permissions, so it can only reach data you can see. Send it as a Bearer token in the Authorization header. Keep keys secret; anyone with a key can act as you. Revoke a key anytime from the same page, which immediately stops it working. Each workspace can have up to 10 active keys.

# API rate limits

The Nimbus API allows 120 requests per minute per API key on the Team plan and 600 per minute on the Business plan. If you exceed the limit you get an HTTP 429 response with a Retry-After header telling you how many seconds to wait. Batch reads where possible and cache results that do not change often. Rate limits are per key, so spreading load across keys does not raise your total allowance.

# Mobile app

The Nimbus mobile app is available for iOS and Android. Sign in with the same account as the web app. The app supports viewing and creating tasks, running the timer, and getting push notifications. Some features such as reports and billing are web-only. The app keeps a local copy so you can view recent tasks offline; changes made offline sync when you reconnect.

# Fixing mobile sync problems

If the mobile app shows out-of-date data, first pull down to refresh. If that does not help, confirm you are online and signed into the correct workspace. Force a full resync from Settings > Sync > Resync in the app. Changes made offline sync when you reconnect; if an offline change conflicts with a newer server change, the server version wins and your change is kept as a comment on the task so nothing is lost.

# Notification settings

Control notifications from Settings > Notifications. Choose per-event whether you get email, in-app, and push notifications, for events like assigned to a task, mentioned in a comment, and task due soon. Due-soon reminders go out 24 hours before the due date by default; you can change this. Set Do Not Disturb hours to pause push notifications. Workspace-wide notification defaults are set by Admins but each person can override them.

# Two-factor authentication (2FA)

Turn on 2FA from Settings > Security > Two-factor authentication. Nimbus supports authenticator apps (TOTP) and, on Business, hardware security keys. When enabled, you enter a 6-digit code from your app after your password. Save the backup codes shown during setup; each can be used once if you lose your device. Admins can require 2FA for the whole workspace. If you are locked out, an Admin can reset your 2FA.

# Data security and privacy

Nimbus encrypts data in transit and at rest. You can choose an EU or US data region when the workspace is created; it cannot be changed later. To request a copy or deletion of your personal data under GDPR, an Owner can use Settings > Privacy > Data request, or contact support. Deleting a workspace removes all its data after the 30-day grace period. We do not sell customer data.

# Deleting a workspace

Only the Owner can delete a workspace, from Settings > Advanced > Delete workspace. Deletion is scheduled after a 30-day grace period, during which the Owner can cancel it from the same page. After the grace period all projects, tasks, time entries, and members lose access and the data is permanently removed. Export anything you want to keep before the grace period ends. An active paid subscription must be canceled first.

# Nimbus is slow or not loading

If Nimbus is slow or a page will not load, first check status.nimbus.example for a known incident. If all is green, hard refresh the page, then try an incognito window to rule out a browser extension. A very large project with thousands of tasks loads faster if you filter or archive completed tasks. The web app supports the latest two versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari; older browsers may be slow.

# Importing data from other tools

Import tasks from a CSV file from Settings > Import. Your CSV needs at least a task title column; optional columns are assignee email, due date (YYYY-MM-DD), status, and project. Rows with an unknown assignee email are imported unassigned. We also have guided importers for Trello and Asana that map boards and lists to projects and sections. Imports over 5,000 rows run in the background and email you when done.
